units.translation: Hesychius: Ξιφίρου λιμήν [the harbor of Xiphirus]: Aeschylus in Glaucus Potnieus (fr. 38. Pontius according to Hermann), the strait. For all these things (all these things in the codex) around Rhegium are of the seasons (of the seasons Musurus). Where Valesius reads τῶν — ὁρίων [of the boundaries], Alberti reads τῶν νεωρίων [of the dockyards].

The name Ξιφίρου [of Xiphirus] is suspect, which seemed to Bernhardy in Annal. Berolin. a. 1828 p. 243 to be corrupted from Ξιφωνίου [of Xiphonius]. Ξιφώνειος λιμήν [the harbor of Xiphonius] is mentioned by Scylax p. 4 (21 ed. Muell.). This conjecture is neither probable in itself and was rejected by Meineke on account of the location of the places, who himself conjectured Ξιφήρους λιμήν [the harbor of Xipherous]: -ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα περὶ Ῥήγιον Ωρίωνος ἔργον [for all these things around Rhegium are the work of Orion] in Philol. vol. 13 p. 511, comparing Diodorus 4, 85. No more certain are the suggestions brought by those whom Schmidt cites: Leutsch in Encyclopaedia Halensis s.v. Glaukos p. 194 and Gaedechens in his commentary on Glaucus the sea-god, published in Berlin in 1860. To me only this seems certain: Ξιφίρου λιμήν [the harbor of Xiphirus], although the sequence of letters in Hesychius demands this, is corrupted from Ξιφήρους λιμήν [the harbor of Xipherous], and ὡρίων [of the seasons] is nothing other than Ὠρίων [Orion]. The gloss is defective at the end, in which perhaps the words of Euripides were mentioned, Ion 1153: Πλειάς μὲν ἤει μεσοπόρου δι᾿ αἰθέρος | ὅ τε ξιφήρης Ωρίων [the Pleiad was passing through the mid-heaven, and sword-bearing Orion], which M. Schmidt compared in Philologus vol. 19 p. 598, who conjectured that the gloss of Hesychius ended with the word Ρήγιον [Rhegium], but that Ωρίων [Orion] remained from another gloss, whose lemma was ξιφήρης Ωρίων [sword-bearing Orion]. Nor does the beginning of the gloss seem intact, since ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα [for all these things] has nothing to refer to. Bernhardy sensed this when he indicated a lacuna before ό πορθμός [the strait]. For Aeschylus without doubt had mentioned other names of places situated in lower Italy besides Ξιφήρους λιμένα [the harbor of Xipherous].
